requirements.requirement: Streaming replication established across node1/node2/node3 with node1 as writable primary and node2/node3 as standbys
requirements.summary: PostgreSQL 15 installed on all three nodes; node2 and node3 were basebackup'd from node1 with pg_basebackup -R and confirmed as standbys via pg_is_in_recovery()=t with identical ledger data. pg_stat_replication on node1 showed both node2 and node3 streaming, later reconfigured to quorum-synchronous (sync_state=quorum) via synchronous_standby_names='ANY 1 (node2, node3)'.

requirements.requirement: When the primary is lost, a standby takes over as the writable primary without losing committed data
requirements.summary: A marker row was inserted and confirmed replicated to both standbys (matching LSNs) immediately before node1 was stopped. node2 was promoted via pg_ctl promote, pg_is_in_recovery() flipped to false, and all pre-failover rows including the marker were confirmed present with zero loss; a subsequent write to node2 succeeded, proving writability.

requirements.requirement: The remaining standby (node3) continues following whichever node is now primary
requirements.summary: node3's primary_conninfo was repointed to node2; PostgreSQL logs show an automatic timeline switch to timeline 2 and resumed streaming, and pg_stat_replication on node2 confirmed node3 streaming in quorum sync.

requirements.requirement: The recovered former primary (node1) comes back as a standby of the current primary
requirements.summary: node1 was rebuilt from node2 via pg_basebackup -R, started with pg_is_in_recovery()=t, confirmed streaming/quorum in node2's pg_stat_replication, and all historical ledger rows were present on node1.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract are directly and coherently evidenced: node1/node2/node3 streaming replication was established with quorum-synchronous commit, node1's simulated loss was followed by a zero-data-loss promotion of node2 (verified via a pre-failover marker row and matching LSNs), node3 correctly followed the new primary via an automatic timeline switch, and node1 was rebuilt and rejoined as a standby of node2. The independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was also executed on all three nodes with matching pre/post boot identities cross-checked against the fixed global lifecycle snapshots (node1: 745be096→cd050683, node2: 151c4aa9→74e4c271, node3: e9250ad1→5a2c71ec), reboot acknowledgements returning before disconnect, and full replication/data/quorum recovery confirmed after each reboot, including a final end-to-end write verified on all three nodes. Along the way the executor encountered and self-corrected two operational missteps (a brief plaintext credential exposure, and a synchronous-commit misconfiguration that caused hung backends/timeouts) plus a missed systemd-enable step on two standbys during the restart sequence, all resolved without lasting negative effect on final functionality.
limitations: The final after_executor package-health check was unavailable (TimeoutError) on all three nodes, so RPM/package consistency cannot be independently confirmed beyond the successful install/verify commands in the timeline.

The replication password was briefly visible in plaintext in one command's stdout (cmd-9ac7d3e37d514e0a); this is a real, if bounded and self-remediated, credential-hygiene lapse that lowers confidence in secret-handling discipline slightly.

Setting synchronous_standby_names before any standby was attached caused multiple 125-second command timeouts and stuck postgres backends that required manual killing; this reflects an ordering mistake during setup, fully corrected but adding noise to the evidence trail.

postgresql-15 was not enabled for boot on node2/node3 initially and had to be fixed reactively during the restart protocol, indicating the initial systemd configuration was incomplete until caught by the restart verification.

operational_hygiene.summary: Overall hygiene is reasonable but shows several self-inflicted issues that required corrective work. (1) The replication password appeared in plaintext in a command's stdout at cmd-9ac7d3e37d514e0a ('sudo cat .../.repl_pw_tmp'); the executor recognized this and rotated the credential multiple times afterward (cmd-6820b52bf0924f05, cmd-444c7e10e16c4206, cmd-293f5fc268c449a1) using scp transfer instead of re-printing it — a bounded, self-corrected exposure rather than a persisted one. (2) Setting synchronous_standby_names on node1 before any standby had joined caused CREATE ROLE statements to hang waiting on synchronous commit, producing five ~125s proxy-timeout failures (cmd-fa53580c76494ef8, cmd-2acbd3ffb9584fe6, cmd-4648b4a6f34746a1, cmd-08b127567388461d, cmd-72f44fec244d403d) and several stuck postgres backend processes that had to be manually killed (cmd-17c9154e32e046ef) after temporarily clearing synchronous_standby_names (cmd-2e240f7833874ee1) and restoring it later (cmd-23b2057608f24090). This was a bounded, fully-reverted troubleshooting detour with no lasting residue. (3) postgresql-15 was found disabled for boot on node2 and node3 partway through the restart protocol and had to be enabled reactively/proactively (cmd-1bd7a585ab1f48a0, cmd-610e0e3f18be4ec5) — a corrective fix rather than an unnecessary mutation, but it reflects an initial gap in the deployment (systemctl enable --now was used for node1 at cmd-ba1d833cc9c542cf but plain 'start' without enable was used for node2/node3 at cmd-f1319ca734ad4f45/cmd-f69189464306417e). (4) Minor residue: /tmp/pg_install.log, /tmp/pg_install2.log, and /tmp/reboot.log remain on all three nodes in the after_executor snapshot — low-severity leftover artifacts that were not cleaned up.
